dedupe_keys.name: usda nass agricultural chemical use database state level pesticide and fertiliser use by commodity 1990 onwards

description: An interactive database of agricultural chemical use in the United States, built from surveys already published by the USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) and consolidated at state level. The Ag Data Commons record says it was created by USDA, the USDA Regional Pest Management Centers and the NSF Center for Integrated Pest Management, with CSREES funding, and that users can search by commodity, year, state and active ingredient for commodity acreage, percent of acres treated, active ingredient per acre per treatment, number of treatments and total active ingredient used. Results show on the web or as downloadable Excel files, with dynamic US maps and graphs; data start in 1990 and were to be updated yearly. It also points to the NASS Chemical Use programme, whose surveys since 2009 are released through Quick Stats with highlights, methodology papers and data tables. The record is in the US public domain (posted to the new Ag Data Commons in February 2024, originally issued in 2015). Coverage is surveyed US states and crops. Caveats: surveys rotate among crops and states, so series have gaps, and whether the yearly updates continued is not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives demand for fertilisers and pesticides by crop and state, to model chemical supply chains to farms and the effect of a plant or port outage. A related catalogue record is the USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer.
